Abstract: Emerging low-altitude services, such as UAV delivery and aerial inspection, increasingly rely on deep neural network (DNN) inference to support timely perception and decision making. Existing studies mainly focus on latency-oriented offloading or isolated resource optimization, while paying limited attention to energy-aware joint orchestration of model partitioning, deployment, and resource allocation for collaborative inference services. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Cloud-Edge-End Adaptive Partitioning and Resource Allocation method for Collaborative Inference(CAPRI). Abstract: For UAV-enabled intelligent applications, e.g., urban monitoring, multi-UAV collaborative inference has becoming a popular paradigm of edge intelligence service. To achieve the service-continuous edge intelligence, we propose a predictive and cost-optimal migration scheme, named Promise, through jointly optimizing across-swarm UAV migration and intra-swarm service migration. To adapt to the dynamics in multi-UAV networks, the system state representations are hierarchically defined and constructed as a graph indicating UAV-swarm relationships. Through extracting the inherent spatiotemporal features in the graph, a lightweight spatiotemporal graph neural network (LST-GNN) is designed to achieve the rolling prediction of migration. For the cost-optimal migration while ensuring the inference service continuity, the migration is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) problem with comprehensive consideration of migration delay, energy consumption, and service interruption duration. To address the state coupling between across-swarm UAV migration and intra-swarm service migration, we decouple the migration problem into a hierarchical decision-making proven as NP-hard, and design a Prediction-Driven Blocked Hungarian (PDBH) algorithm to offer promising solutions. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed Promise scheme.
